A 49-year-old male with no prior medical history or medications is brought to the emergency
department following a 3-minute seizure episode. His roommate discovered him unresponsive in bed
with rhythmic movements of all extremities. Upon evaluation, the patient is lethargic but oriented. His
vital signs show: temperature 98.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure 150/94 mmHg, pulse 88/min, and
respirations 14/min. Neurological examination reveals equal and reactive pupils, full strength in all

extremities, and normal deep-tendon reflexes. Basic laboratory tests including electrolytes, glucose,
and complete blood count have been ordered. What should be the next step in this patient's
management? Answer Choices: (A) Urine toxicology (B) Lumbar puncture (C) Start antiepileptic
medication (D) Neurology consultation (E) Sleep-deprived EEG (F) Electroencephalography (EEG) (G)
Serum alcohol level (H) Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of brain (I) Electroencephalogram (EEG)
(J) Computed tomography (CT) of brain
